newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark hints at compromise over Helms-Burton plan.
newsitem.headline: Denmark hints at compromise over Helms-Burton plan.

text.p: Denmark, poised to veto a planned EU defence against U.S. anti-Cuba trade laws, says its objections are purely technical and alternative means to make an response are being explored.

"Denmark is not against the European Union taking precautionary measures against the USA, it's just that we cannot accept the use of article 235 (of the EU's founding Treaty of Rome)," Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen told the Danish news agency Ritzau overnight.
"I know that others are trying to find an alternative basis on which to proceed," he added.
The article allows the EU to act in policy areas not specified elsewhere in the treaty and is seen with suspicion by governments wary of ceding too much authority to Brussels.

Diplomats say that the other 14 EU member states have nevertheless accepted the use of article 235 in this case but Denmark has been made especially sensitive to issues of sovereignty by a pending court case on the issue.

A group of citizens have filed suit saying that Denmark's signature of the Maastricht treaty contravenes the national constitution by transferring too much political and judicial authority to supranational EU institutions.
Danish officials deny that their veto threat has any connection with the court action, in which preliminary hearings begin next week.
